title: On opportunities and challenges of large multimodal foundation models in education
extended_summary:
This perspective paper examines the emerging role of large multimodal foundation models (LMFMs) in education and asks how these systems differ from earlier large language models in their educational uses and risks. The authors frame LMFMs as models that can process and generate not only text, but also speech, images, and video, and they discuss how this multimodality expands opportunities for learning, teaching, research, and educational software development.

The paper is not an empirical intervention study; instead, it provides a conceptual overview of likely use cases. For learners, it highlights possibilities such as personalized learning assistants, multimodal feedback, support for language learning, image generation and interpretation, help with experimentation, code generation, and accessibility features for students with disabilities. For educators, it discusses lesson planning, classroom activity design, assessment creation and grading, dashboards, teacher training simulations, and administrative support. It also distinguishes teacher-facing uses from student-facing tutoring tools by emphasizing educator workflow support, task design, and feedback generation rather than direct instruction alone.

The paper is situated in K-12 and higher-education discussions broadly, but it does not report a specific participant sample, school setting, or country because it is a theoretical perspective. Its main conclusion is that LMFMs could substantially improve personalization, engagement, and efficiency in education, but only if educators and institutions address major concerns including hallucinations, bias, privacy, unequal access, overreliance, and the need for AI literacy and human oversight.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based conversational generative AI family used for text generation, multimodal understanding, and task-oriented assistance via prompts and APIs.
identified_tools.use_case: This perspective discusses ChatGPT and GPT-4-Turbo/GPTs as teacher-facing and student-facing generative AI tools for lesson planning, assessment creation, feedback, tutoring, data analysis, and educational application development, but does not report an empirical evaluation in this paper.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a perspective article rather than an empirical study, systematic review, or meta-analysis. It provides conceptual discussion of opportunities and challenges without reporting original data or evaluated outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper argues that ChatGPT/GPT-based tools may have broad educational utility, especially for lesson planning, feedback, and assessment support, but it does not present measured effects. Because no outcome data are reported, empirical impact is not established.
